report.summary: The bug in the request is already fixed: commit f1b8a67 (#63) treats SandboxFileError ENOENT as an absent file, and the test 'runs when a login file is missing, as for an owner without a Codex login' covers it. This diff goes further and replaces that narrow check with `.catch(() => null)`. Every readFile failure now counts as 'absent': permission errors, a path that is a directory, timeouts, a stopped container, transport errors. The check that compares protected file hashes before and after a run now passes whenever it can't read a file. That weakens the RUN_ACCESS_VIOLATION guard in 08/01 without changing the spec, and no test covers the wider behavior.

findings.text: Blocking: the guard now passes when it can't read a file. Any readFile rejection becomes `null`, and `null` is also how the guard records a missing file. Example: a login file is absent before the run (an owner without a Codex login). The agent creates /home/tempo/.codex/auth.json as a directory, as a mode-000 file, or as a symlink to a path it can't read. The after-run read then fails, the hash is null, it matches the before value, and RUN_ACCESS_VIOLATION is never raised. A temporary container or RPC failure during the after-run check also hides a change. The old code threw RUN_ACCESS_VIOLATION here on purpose ('any other failure stays RUN_ACCESS_VIOLATION'). Keep the narrow `SandboxFileError.is(cause) && cause.code === "ENOENT"` check, or name any other error codes that really mean 'not set up' one by one, and keep throwing on everything else.

The request ('a login the owner never set up must not block a run') is already met on the base branch. ENOENT is treated as absent and runs.cases.ts tests it. The diff doesn't name a case that still fails, such as a different error code from the SDK. Without one, the only effect is that other errors now pass silently. If there is a real failing case (for example, the SDK reporting ENOTDIR when ~/.codex itself is missing), handle that code by name and add a test that reproduces it.

The diff changes no tests, and no test checks that a non-ENOENT read failure is handled correctly. Rule 14 requires a test for every op step. Rule 16 requires a spec update when behavior changes, and docs/08 and docs/01 still say that changes to protected login/config files fail the run.
If the ENOENT check is restored, the SandboxFileError import removed here has to come back as well.

args.command: cat apps/tempo/src/agents/protected-files.ts && grep -rn "RUN_ACCESS_VIOLATION\|protected login\|Protected login" docs | head -30; grep -rln "protectedFileHashes\|ENOENT" apps/tempo | head

grep -n "protected\|ENOENT\|RUN_ACCESS" apps/tempo/test/worker/runs.cases.ts apps/tempo/src/do/workspace/runs.ts | head -30; grep -n -i "protected\|unreadable\|ENOENT" docs/IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md | head; git log --oneline -5 -- apps/tempo/src/agents/protected-files.ts
sed -n 270,320p apps/tempo/test/worker/runs.cases.ts; git show --stat HEAD | head; git show f1b8a67 --stat | head -20
